headline: Brazil Central Bank Sells $1 Billion Spot Reserves as Real Depreciates Near R$5.90
summary: Brazil's central bank conducted a spot auction selling US$1 billion in reserves to support the real, though the exchange rate remained under pressure near R$5.90 per dollar.
why: The Central Bank of Brazil intervenes in foreign exchange spot markets to curb excessive currency volatility and manage domestic dollar supply.

impacts.name: Brazilian Real
impacts.why: Spot reserve interventions by the central bank targeted sustained currency depreciation pressure.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Central bank dollar reserve sales were absorbed by high market demand, keeping the dollar near R$5.90.
